chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Ali ibn Abi al-Mughira, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom! Can one derive any benefit from a dead animal?' He said: 'No.'

I said: 'It has reached us that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a dead sheep and said: What prevented the owners of this sheep, since they could not benefit from its flesh, from benefiting from its hide?'

He said: 'That was a sheep belonging to Sawda bint Zam'a, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). It was an emaciated sheep from whose flesh no benefit could be derived. They left it until it died. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: What prevented its owners, since they could not benefit from its flesh, from benefiting from its hide — meaning, by slaughtering it.'

key_terms.إِهَابِهَا: Its hide/skin (ihab) — the untanned skin of an animal; becomes lawful only through slaughter or tanning
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةُ: Mayta — an animal that has died without lawful slaughter; ritually impure and forbidden for most uses
key_terms.تُذَكَّى: Tadhkiya — ritual slaughter according to Islamic law, which renders the animal's parts lawful

ai.seo_question: Can one use the skin or hide of a dead animal in Islam according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: A companion asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether any use may be made of a dead animal (mayta) and receives a categorical 'No'. When the questioner cites a hadith about the Prophet recommending use of a dead sheep's hide, the Imam clarifies the historical context: the sheep in question belonged to the Prophet's wife Sawda bint Zam'a, was left to die due to extreme emaciation, and the Prophet's remark was a reproach — the owners should have slaughtered the sheep before its death, making its skin lawfully usable. This hadith establishes that benefit from mayta is generally forbidden, and that the Prophet's statement implied the owners should have performed ritual slaughter (tadhkiya) while the animal was still alive.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Ibn Mahboub, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Ali Bin Abu Al Mugra who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The dead, can one benefit from it with anything’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

I said, ‘It has reached us that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> passed by a dead sheep, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What was upon the owners of this sheep that when they could not benefit by its flesh, that they did not benefit from its skin?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That was a sheep of Sawda Bin Zam’at, wife of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and it was thin and weak, could not be benefit by its flesh. So she left it until it was dead. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What was upon the owners of this sheep that when they could not benefit by its flesh, that they did not benefit from its skin?’ i.e., slaughtering it’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Ali ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, is it permissible to benefit from dead animals?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not permissible.’

I then said, ‘It is narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, that he (the Messenger of Allah) passed by a dead sheep and said, “What was wrong with the owners of this sheep? If they could not benefit from its flesh why did they not benefit from its skin?”’

He (the Imam) said, ‘That sheep belonged to Sawdah daughter of Zam‘ah, wife of the Holy Prophet. The sheep was very skinny and weak and its flesh was not useful; so they left it until it died. The Messenger of Allah then said, “What was wrong with the owners of this sheep. If they could not benefit from its flesh why did they not benefit from its skin?”’
